name: Absinthe Green
lede: Absinthe Green is a moderate yellow green from Ridgway's 1912 plates, filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, and strongly overrepresented in Impressionist and Rajput painting in our archive.

sections.title: A 1912 plate, a 1955 filing
sections.body:
Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* (1912) places this hue at plate XXXI, hue 29″, a scan of an aged printed page and so only approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it as a grayish greenish yellow [1]. Our sources do not document why the name invokes the drink absinthe rather than simply describing the hue; that connection is left unconfirmed here [2].

Its closest named relatives are [[deep-chrysolite-green]], almost indistinguishable at 2.9 units, and [[neva-green]], a touch more vivid [3].

Further out are [[lily-green]], darker at 3.5 units, and [[light-olive]], more vivid at 3.6 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Absinthe Green covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 87 works, two-thirds of that as highlight rather than mid-tone or shadow [4]. Auguste Renoir is the strongest painter match, present in five of his ninety-six archived paintings, over fourteen times the expected rate, and the style of Rajput painting carries it at over fourteen times the archive's rate too [4]. It most often shares a canvas with khaki and sage [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented; possibly evokes the drink absinthe, but our sources do not confirm this
